📊 Twice-yearly disclosures on the horizon

There’s growing talk that quarterly earnings updates could be swapped for disclosures twice a year. The idea traces back to a 2018 SEC push, pitched as a way to trim costs and give companies a bit more breathing room.

- Fewer filings, less quarterly pressure, more room to invest and grow.
- The flip side is simple: investors would hear from companies less often, information gaps could widen, and big moves might only show up after earnings.

This isn’t policy yet. If momentum builds, the debate will come down to cost savings versus transparency. Markets adapt, but uncertainty is usually priced in.
